title: Metastability-resolution TRNG (latch/flip-flop settling-time entropy source)
topology: A bistable element — a cross-coupled latch, a flip-flop, or a pair of cross-coupled inverters — is deliberately driven into its metastable balance point (both nodes at roughly the trip voltage) and then released, letting thermal noise decide which of the two stable states it resolves to. Because the resolution direction from a near-balanced start is governed by circuit noise, the resolved bit is random. Practical designs add a control loop that nudges the latch back toward true metastability (e.g. trimming the differential offset or the timing of the balancing pulse) so process mismatch and drift do not bias the element permanently into one state, keeping the entropy rate high. Unlike the oscillator-jitter sources, entropy here comes from a single settling event rather than accumulated phase noise, giving a compact, fast-per-sample digital entropy cell.
spec_class: hardware security primitive — true-random-number-generator (TRNG) noise/entropy source for cryptographic key generation, nonces, and DRBG seeding, where a compact all-digital entropy cell with a metastability-quality feedback loop is wanted; the design must supply raw entropy plus health-testable conditioning, not any analog-precision spec

pdk_portability.notes: The cross-coupled-latch metastability cell is portable to any CMOS PDK, including sky130 core devices (sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 / pfet_01v8) and standard-cell flip-flops. What is PDK-specific is the latch's intrinsic offset and resolution time constant (set by device mismatch, gain, and load), which determine how strong a balancing/trim control is needed to hold the cell near metastability and how deep the metastable window is. The offset-cancellation or metastability-tracking loop must be re-tuned against sky130 mismatch statistics and corners; a design ported without re-characterization will bias toward one state and lose entropy. Estimate SP 800-90B min-entropy on real silicon, since deterministic offset drift can mimic — but is not — noise-driven resolution.

sizing_approach: Size the cross-coupled pair for a short resolution time constant (high loop gain, light load) so each entropy event is fast, but not so aggressive that intrinsic offset dominates the noise and pins the outcome. The central trade-off is metastability depth versus device mismatch: the noise-driven region must be reachable and held against the latch's own systematic offset, so pair the core cell with a calibration/feedback path (offset trim or balancing-pulse timing control) whose resolution is fine enough to null the worst-corner mismatch and keep the resolved-bit bias within the budget the downstream conditioner can correct. Use matched device sizing and layout to minimize the systematic offset the loop must cancel. Size for the worst mismatch corner (largest offset, fastest resolution where noise has least time to act) and rely on continuous health tests plus the tracking loop to maintain entropy as temperature and supply drift.
layout_idioms: tight common-centroid / interdigitated matching of the cross-coupled devices to minimize the systematic offset that would otherwise pin the latch to one state and kill entropy
symmetric, balanced routing of the two regenerative nodes (equal load, equal coupling) so neither node has a deterministic head start out of the metastable point
guard ring and clean local decoupling around the latch so supply/substrate transients do not deterministically steer the resolution and masquerade as entropy

expose a raw-noise-source tap (pre-conditioning) and the metastability-loop control state to a test path for SP 800-90B silicon validation, and keep the sample/reset timing generator adjacent to the cell so the balancing pulse is not skewed by routing

source.citation: C. Tokunaga, D. Blaauw, and T. Mudge, "True Random Number Generator With a Metastability-Based Quality Control," IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits, vol. 43, no. 1, pp. 78-85, Jan. 2008. Health-testing/architecture guidance: E. Barker et al., NIST Special Publication 800-90B, "Recommendation for the Entropy Sources Used for Random Bit Generation," January 2018.
source.license_or_openness: Tokunaga-Blaauw-Mudge is a peer-reviewed IEEE journal paper cited here for its metastability-resolution TRNG topology and the metastability-tracking quality-control methodology only (no figures or text reproduced) — case 2, restated ideas only, IEEE Xplore subscription for the full PDF. NIST SP 800-90B is a public-domain U.S. government standard, freely downloadable. No proprietary or NDA'd data is recorded.

notes: The metastability-quality feedback loop is what distinguishes a robust metastable TRNG from a fragile one: without it, process mismatch and slow drift pull the latch off its balance point and the bit stops being random even though the circuit still toggles. As with all raw entropy sources, condition the output (vetted conditioning function or extractor) and run always-on SP 800-90B health tests (Repetition Count Test, Adaptive Proportion Test) on the raw resolved bits with a raw-tap access path for silicon validation. Compared with the oscillator-jitter sources (ring-oscillator-jitter-trng, multi-ro-xor-entropy-source), this cell is more compact and faster per event but more sensitive to systematic offset, so its calibration loop is the critical design element.

artifacts.notes: From-scratch netlist (real sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8/pfet_01v8 devices, not behavioral): a cross-coupled inverter pair held equalized near its own switching threshold by a transmission gate shorting its two nodes, then released to resolve. Because a single deterministic SPICE run has no thermal noise, one inverter's pull-down NMOS is drawn a deterministic 5% wider than the other's as a stand-in for the noise that decides a real cell's outcome -- the same technique sram-power-up-puf/sram_cell_powerup.spice and ro-puf/ro_puf.spice use for their own mismatch/noise stand-ins. The resolved state measured here (q low / qb high) is a property of this injected asymmetry's sign, not a prediction of any real trial's outcome, and no entropy/min-entropy claim is made. This testbench also does NOT implement the metastability-quality feedback/tracking loop this entry's own sizing_approach and notes call load-bearing for a robust design -- it demonstrates only the release-and-resolve mechanism the loop would operate on. See measured.notes for the same disclosure.

measured.notes: Real sky130A device models (volare-fetched, open_pdks), not behavioral elements. Reproduce with `klt sim examples/kb/metastability-trng/request.json`. The cell is held equalized (transmission gate closed) from t=0 to t=2ns; vmeta_q_v/vmeta_qb_v/vmeta_sep_v are sampled at t=1.9ns, just before release, and confirm the cell is sitting near its shared switching threshold (both ~0.85V, ~2mV apart) rather than at either rail -- i.e. actually at the metastable balance point this entry's topology describes, not merely claimed to be. Release happens at t=2ns (t_release); resolve_delay_s is the time from release to qb crossing back through 0.9V (t_resolve_qb), and vq_final_v/vqb_final_v are the settled full-rail resolution at t=5.9ns. The resolved polarity (q low, qb high) is a property of the injected pull-down-width asymmetry's sign described in artifacts.notes, not a prediction of any real trial's outcome -- on real silicon the outcome is thermal-noise-driven and differs trial to trial. NO metastability-quality feedback/tracking loop is implemented (see artifacts.notes), and NO entropy/min-entropy claim is made or measurable from one deterministic run.
